claims.source_quote_ar: ففيه التفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب.
claims.claim_ar: التفات (انتقال) من الغيبة إلى الخطاب في الانتقال من بيان حكم عام حول النسخ إلى مخاطبة مباشرة (أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ) لزيادة التوكيد والانتباه.
claims.claim_en: Iltifat (shift from third-person/general discourse to direct address): the verse moves from a general statement about abrogation to direct address (أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ), increasing emphasis and engaging the hearer.
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted source states the rhetorical principle ('turning from ghayba to khitab') generally; it is not explicitly discussing S2:106 in that excerpt, so application to this specific verse should be reviewed.
claims.rhetorical_effect: heightens attention and moral responsibility by addressing the audience directly after a doctrinal statement

claims.claim_ar: جملة تأكيدية تالية تعمل كبيان وشرح لما قبلها — هنا التأكيد على قدرة الله يوضّح ويقوّي ما قيل عن النسخ والإتيان بخير أو مثلها.
claims.claim_en: Explanatory reinforcement (fasl/wasl): the following clause serves as an explicative clarification or reinforcement of what precedes it — here, the affirmation of God's power clarifies and strengthens the statement about abrogation and replacement.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source fragment uses the term 'بيان' for explanatory clauses; the excerpt does not cite S2:106 directly, so mapping this explanatory function onto the verse is inferential and should be checked.
claims.rhetorical_effect: provides assurance and logical grounding (i.e., because God is capable, abrogation/replacement is under His control), reducing doubts and reinforcing trust

claims.claim_ar: وجود مقابلة/تباين بين فعل النسخ والإتيان ببديل أفضل أو مثله يبرز تغيّر الحكم ويعطي وزناً لعملية الاستبدال؛ الآية تستخدم هذه المقابلة لتبيان حكمة الله وقدرته.
claims.claim_en: Contrast / muqabalah: the verse establishes a contrast between the abrogated verse and what replaces it (something better or like it), underscoring change of ruling and the wisdom/omnipotence behind that change.
claims.needs_review_reason: Source discusses how change of attribute/status signals a substantive change (contrast) in meaning; it is a general principle and not an explicit commentary on S2:106 in the provided excerpt, so verification is advised.
claims.rhetorical_effect: frames abrogation as purposeful and positive (replacement by better or similar), reducing perceived arbitrariness and reassuring the listener
